+#   Citation validity first (both clauses of the new rule): a cited line is positive;
+#   a cited range is ordered (a <= b, the parser orders it); when the defect's file
+#   exists under the head directory the range must lie inside it (1 <= a <= b <= its
+#   line count), else it credits nothing. A cited range wider than 25 lines credits
+#   only through its first line. The two _pm3 results keep the 1.2.0 rule exactly (no
+#   validity rule, no range cap), so recall_pm3_v1 reproduces a 1.2.x grade.
+#   Detection: a valid citation (path, a, b) detects defect d when its path matches d's
+#   file and (i) [a, b] lies within ±3 of any site (unchanged), OR (ii) same scope: the
+#   enclosing definition of the site in head/<file>, identified by its HEADER LINE
+#   NUMBER (never its name), equals the enclosing definition of any cited line in
+#   [a, b]. Definition headers: bash (.sh, .bash, or a bash/sh shebang)
+#   `^\s*(function\s+)?NAME\s*\(\)\s*\{?` and `^\s*function\s+NAME\s*\{`; python
+#   `^\s*def NAME\(`; bats `^@test "…"` plus the bash forms; markdown `#` headings
+#   (the nearest preceding heading's section). A definition runs from its header to
+#   the line before the next header at the same or lower indentation (markdown: the
+#   same or a higher heading level), else to the end of the file, and no further than
+#   its own end (end-of-definition detection): bash and bats — the first `}` line at
+#   the header's indentation (a one-line `f() { …; }` ends on its header); python —

+def expand(tok, vars_):

+# _sm_copy_source <source-tree> → the tree's HEAD (40 hex), "<sha>-dirty" when its .claude/
+# has uncommitted or untracked changes (the copy is then not the commit), else "unknown"
+_sm_copy_source() {
+  local tree="$1" head dirty
+  head="$(git -C "$tree" rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null)" || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  [[ "$head" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  dirty="$(git -C "$tree" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- .claude 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p')" || dirty="?"
+  if [[ -n "$dirty" ]]; then printf '%s-dirty' "$head"; else printf '%s' "$head"; fi
+}

# the cycle-131 toggles and the eval config variant).
# =============================================================================

[[ "${_SANDBOX_MOUNT_LOADED:-}" == "true" ]] && return 0
_SANDBOX_MOUNT_LOADED=true

_SM_LIB_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_SM_REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$_SM_LIB_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"

_sm_err() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; }

# _sm_sha256 <file>... prints "<hex>  <file>" lines, the sha256sum output shape.
# Python hashlib, not compat-lib's sha256_portable: the eval workflow runs the
# harness as the trusted copy against a PR's .claude/, so no harness script
# sources .claude/ code (eval.yml "Validate grader trust boundary"); run-arms.sh
# hashes the corpus the same way.
_sm_sha256() {
  python3 -I -c '
import hashlib, sys
for p in sys.argv[1:]:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(p, "rb") as f:
        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(b)
    print(h.hexdigest() + "  " + p)' "$@"
}

# _sm_evidence <key> <value> — one key=value line to the evidence sink.
_sm_evidence() {
  local line="$1=${2//$'\n'/ }"
  if [[ -n "${ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
  else
    local fd="${SANDBOX_MOUNT_EVIDENCE_FD:-1}"
    [[ "$fd" =~ ^[0-9]$ ]] || fd=1
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >&"$fd"
  fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
mount_prompt_surface() {
  local ws="$1" tree="$2" skill="${3:-}"
  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "mount_prompt_surface: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
  [[ -d "$tree/.claude" ]] || { _sm_err "mount_prompt_surface: prompt tree has no .claude/: $tree"; return 2; }
  if [[ "$skill" == "-" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$ws/.claude"
    cp -a "$tree/.claude/." "$ws/.claude/" || { _sm_err "mount_prompt_surface: copying .claude/ failed"; return 2; }
    printf '@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md\n' > "$ws/CLAUDE.md"
    if [[ -f "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then cp "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" "$ws/.loa.config.yaml"; fi
    _sm_evidence mount "tree"
    return 0
  fi
  case "$skill" in */*|.*|'') _sm_err "invalid skill name '$skill'"; return 2 ;; esac
  local skill_src="$tree/.claude/skills/$skill"
  [[ -f "$skill_src/SKILL.md" ]] || { _sm_err "prompt tree $tree has no .claude/skills/$skill/SKILL.md"; return 2; }
  mkdir -p "$ws/.claude/skills" "$ws/.claude/loa"

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# evals/tests/sandbox-mount.bats — cycle-131 Sprint 263 Task 1.1 (PRD FR-1 AC 1, AC 5;
+# FR-5 AC 1; SDD §5.2 overlay_answer_paths / check_mount_closed, D-1.1, D-5.x)
+#
+# evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh's closed mount on a fixture-shaped sandbox: a
+# throwaway source repository (the pinned Loa tree: a head commit, then a fix commit
+# that is the pin), a PR fixture (head.diff, head/, base/, fixture.yaml) whose head.diff
+# carries every path shape (modified, added, deleted, renamed, a quoted path with a
+# space, a symlink in head, a path outside .claude/, a removed hunk line that looks like
+# a header, a binary hunk), and a sandbox built as pipeline-run.sh builds it (pr/ copied,
+# a base commit, the whole .claude/ mounted). Also the cycle-131 toggles (bare_model,
+# dissent, oracle_open) and the eval config variant. No model call, no docker.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+  LIB="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sm.XXXXXX")"
+  SRC="$T/src" FX="$T/fx" W="$T/ws"
+  export ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE="$T/ev.txt"; : > "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
+  make_source
+  make_fixture
+  make_ws
+}
+
+teardown() {
+  chmod -R u+rwx "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
+  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
+  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+g() { git -C "$1" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t -c commit.gpgsign=false "${@:2}"; }
+
+# the pinned Loa tree: commit H (= the PR's head_commit) then commit F (the fix, the pin)
+make_source() {
+  mkdir -p "$SRC/.claude/scripts" "$SRC/.claude/data" "$SRC/.claude/loa" "$SRC/.claude/skills/s1" "$SRC/lib"
+  printf 'mod head\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"
+  printf 'added head\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/added.sh"
+  printf 'new name head\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/new name.sh"
+  printf 'xy head\n' > "$SRC/.claude/data/x y.txt"
+  printf 'fixonly head\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/fixonly.sh"
+  printf 'skill pinned\n' > "$SRC/.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md"
+  printf 'loa\n' > "$SRC/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+  printf 'outside head\n' > "$SRC/lib/outside.sh"
+  printf '{"files":{}}\n' > "$SRC/.claude/checksums.json"
+  chmod +x "$SRC/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"
+  ( cd "$SRC" && git init -q && g . add -A && g . commit -qm head )
+  H="$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse HEAD)"
+  # the fix commit: later versions of PR paths and of a path the PR never touched
+  printf 'mod LATER fixed\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"
+  printf 'added LATER fixed\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/added.sh"
+  printf 'deleted LATER restored\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/deleted.sh"
+  printf 'new name LATER\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/new name.sh"
+  printf 'xy LATER\n' > "$SRC/.claude/data/x y.txt"
+  printf 'fixonly LATER fixed\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/fixonly.sh"
+  printf '{"files":{"later":1}}\n' > "$SRC/.claude/checksums.json"
+  ( cd "$SRC" && g . add -A && g . commit -qm fix )
+  F="$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse HEAD)"
+}
+
+# the PR fixture (immutable in production: evals/fixtures/review-prs/pr-NN/)
+make_fixture() {
+  mkdir -p "$FX/head/.claude/scripts" "$FX/head/.claude/data" "$FX/head/.claude/skills/s1" "$FX/head/lib" \
+           "$FX/base/.claude/scripts" "$FX/base/.claude/data" "$FX/base/lib"
+  printf 'mod head\n' > "$FX/head/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"; chmod +x "$FX/head/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"
+  printf 'mod base\n' > "$FX/base/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"
+  printf 'added head\n' > "$FX/head/.claude/scripts/added.sh"
+  printf 'deleted base\n' > "$FX/base/.claude/scripts/deleted.sh"

        regions.append((fr["file"], int(fr["start"]) - 3, int(fr["end"]) + 3))

        continue
findings = sorted(set(cites))
refuted = [c for c in findings

if planted:

+    [ "$(_adv_budget_effective 0 10)" = "12" ]     # ceil(12.0)
+    [ "$(_adv_budget_effective 0 11)" = "14" ]     # ceil(13.2)
+    [ "$(_adv_budget_effective 0 214)" = "257" ]   # ceil(256.8)

+    s3_config "hounfour:

+        [ "$(yq eval '.flatline_protocol.security_audit.budget_scale // "absent"' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml")" = "absent" ]
+    fi

+  providers:
+    openai:
+      models:
+        fixture-scale:
+          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 100000000, output_per_mtok: 0}
+flatline_protocol:
+  code_review:
+    enabled: true
+    model: fixture-scale
+    budget_cents: 0
+    timeout_seconds: 30

+    budget_scale: diff"
+    result=$(s3_run review)

+    grep -q "budget: estimate [0-9]*c over 2 planned voice(s) (primary fixture-scale [0-9]*c, companion claude-headless [0-9]*c)" "$T/stderr.log"
+    grep -qx "fixture-scale" "$CALLS"
+    grep -qx "claude-headless" "$CALLS"
+    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.companion_voice.planned' <<<"$result")" = "true" ]
+    [ "$(jq -c '.metadata | {budget_scale, budget_cents_max}' <<<"$result")" = '{"budget_scale":"diff","budget_cents_max":600}' ]

+    local est eff

+@test "NRM-72 adversarial-finding.schema.json documents anchor_line / anchor_line_end as optional integers (minimum 1) and validates a finding with and without them" {
+    local schema="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/schemas/adversarial-finding.schema.json"
+    [ "$(jq -c '."$defs".finding.properties.anchor_line | {type, minimum}' "$schema")" = '{"type":"integer","minimum":1}' ]
+    [ "$(jq -c '."$defs".finding.properties.anchor_line_end | {type, minimum}' "$schema")" = '{"type":"integer","minimum":1}' ]
+    jq -e '."$defs".finding.properties.anchor_line.description | startswith("head-file line of the finding (cycle-131)")' "$schema" >/dev/null
+    jq -e '."$defs".finding.required | index("anchor_line") == null and index("anchor_line_end") == null' "$schema" >/dev/null
+    # a stdlib check of the subset the finding definition uses (required, type, enum, minimum, minLength, pattern,
+    # additionalProperties: false) — the schema is a documentation contract, so no third-party validator is assumed
+    run python3 -I - "$schema" <<'PY'
+import json, re, sys
+d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8'))["$defs"]["finding"]
+def ok(f):
+    if any(k not in f for k in d["required"]): return "missing required"
+    if d.get("additionalProperties") is False and any(k not in d["properties"] for k in f): return "extra key"
+    for k, v in f.items():
+        p = d["properties"][k]
+        t = p.get("type")
+        if t == "integer" and not (isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool)): return k + ": not an integer"
+        if t == "string" and not isinstance(v, str): return k + ": not a string"
+        if "minimum" in p and v < p["minimum"]: return k + ": below minimum"
+        if "enum" in p and v not in p["enum"]: return k + ": not in enum"
+        if "minLength" in p and len(v) < p["minLength"]: return k + ": too short"
+        if "pattern" in p and not re.search(p["pattern"], v): return k + ": pattern"
+        if "oneOf" in p and not any(v in o.get("enum", []) for o in p["oneOf"]): return k + ": oneOf"
+    return ""
+base = {"id": "DISS-001", "severity": "BLOCKING", "category": "error-handling", "description": "d", "failure_mode": "f",
+        "anchor": "x.sh:fn", "anchor_type": "function"}
+cases = [(base, ""), (dict(base, anchor_line=12), ""), (dict(base, anchor_line=12, anchor_line_end=15), ""),
+         (dict(base, anchor_line=0), "anchor_line: below minimum"), (dict(base, anchor_line="12"), "anchor_line: not an integer"),
+         (dict(base, anchor_line=1.5), "anchor_line: not an integer"), (dict(base, anchor_line_end=True), "anchor_line_end: not an integer")]
+bad = [(c, ok(c), want) for c, want in cases if ok(c) != want]
+print("\n".join(f"{c} -> {got!r}, want {want!r}" for c, got, want in bad) or "all ok")
+sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
+PY

+@test "NRM-74 both dissent wire schemas carry anchor_line / anchor_line_end as nullable integers inside the strict subset: a finding with integer lines validates, one with null lines validates, one without the keys does not (strict mode lists every property as required), and nothing else in the finding object changed" {
+    local k w
+    for k in review audit; do
+        w="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/schemas/wire/dissent-$k.wire.json"
+        # the two fields: integer or null (the API-safe optional — W2 needs required == properties, W3 forbids minimum)
+        [ "$(jq -c '.properties.findings.items.properties.anchor_line' "$w")" = '{"anyOf":[{"type":"integer"},{"type":"null"}]}' ] || { echo "$k: anchor_line"; return 1; }
+        [ "$(jq -c '.properties.findings.items.properties.anchor_line_end' "$w")" = '{"anyOf":[{"type":"integer"},{"type":"null"}]}' ] || { echo "$k: anchor_line_end"; return 1; }
+        jq -e '.properties.findings.items | (.required | index("anchor_line") != null and index("anchor_line_end") != null) and .additionalProperties == false' "$w" >/dev/null || { echo "$k: not required or not closed"; return 1; }
+        # the rest of the finding object is the cycle-130 shape: the same eleven other properties, all required
+        [ "$(jq -c '.properties.findings.items | [(.properties | keys - ["anchor_line", "anchor_line_end"]), (.required - ["anchor_line", "anchor_line_end"] | sort)]' "$w")" \
+          = '[["anchor","anchor_type","category","cross_file_justification","description","failure_mode","id","scope","severity","suggested_fix","trigger_anchor"],["anchor","anchor_type","category","cross_file_justification","description","failure_mode","id","scope","severity","suggested_fix","trigger_anchor"]]' ] \
+          || { echo "$k: another property or required entry changed"; return 1; }
+    done
+    # validation of enforced-shape findings against each wire schema — a stdlib check of the subset the wire schemas use (type,
+    # enum, anyOf, required, additionalProperties: false), then the full validator where the host has one
+    run python3 -I - "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/schemas/wire" <<'PY'
+import json, os, sys
+def check(node, v):

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 259 Task 2.6
# (SDD §3.6, §5.7, D-4.7, D-4.8; sprint.md AC-2.3, AC-2.5, AC-2.6; PRD AC-6.1/6.2/6.4;
# DEC-0401, DEC-0413, DEC-0414, DEC-0420, DEC-0491, DEC-0493)
#
# evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh grades run directories shaped like pipeline-run.sh's
# (sandbox/ with its own .git, snapshots/<LABEL>.bundle + index.json, transcripts/,
# eval/, meta/). docker is fixtures/docker-stub.sh through a wrapper that sets
# DOCKER_STUB_PATH to $T/bin, where `python3` drops the image-only -I/-s flags (the
# host's pytest lives in the user site) and `bats` is the operator's bats-core. The
# tasks are built in a temporary suite root; the smoke self-checks run on a frozen copy
# of grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke/.
# =============================================================================

# The bats that grades bats-tested tasks: LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN, else the first bats on PATH, else the
# operator's bats-core checkout (Bridgebuilder PR #1283 F-HIGH: a hard-coded dotfiles path dangled on CI).
# Inside a bats run, PATH carries bats-core's libexec; a grading bats must be a real entry point, so
# the first PATH candidate outside a libexec/ directory wins.
find_bats() {
  local c
  [[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN:-}" ]] && { printf '%s' "$LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN"; return; }
  for c in $(type -aP bats 2>/dev/null); do case "$c" in */libexec/*) ;; *) printf '%s' "$c"; return ;; esac; done
  printf '%s' "$HOME/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats"
}
BATS_BIN="$(find_bats)"
# The python3 that runs pytest for the grader: the one on PATH (actions/setup-python on CI, the
# system interpreter here), never a hard-coded /usr/bin/python3.
PY3_BIN="$(command -v python3)"

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  GRADER="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh"
  SMOKE="$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ag.XXXXXX")"
  S="$T/suite"
  export LOA_EVAL_ALLOW_HOST_GRADING=1   # grader 1.2.0 (LOW-A1): host mode is opt-in; AG-28 unsets it
  make_bin
  make_bf_py
  make_bf_sh
  make_rf_py
  make_rc
}

teardown() {
  chmod -R u+rwx "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
}

make_bin() {
  local ub
  ub="$(python3 -c 'import site; print(site.getuserbase())')"
  mkdir -p "$T/bin" "$T/dlog"
  cat > "$T/bin/python3" <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# the image's python3 stand-in: the image has pytest on its own path; the host's is in the user site
while [[ \$# -gt 0 ]]; do case "\$1" in -I|-s|-P) shift ;; *) break ;; esac; done
exec env PYTHONUSERBASE="$ub" "$PY3_BIN" "\$@"

# =============================================================================

# The bats that grades bats-tested tasks: LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN, else the first bats on PATH, else the
# operator's bats-core checkout (Bridgebuilder PR #1283 F-HIGH: a hard-coded dotfiles path dangled on CI).
# Inside a bats run, PATH carries bats-core's libexec; a grading bats must be a real entry point, so
# the first PATH candidate outside a libexec/ directory wins.
find_bats() {
  local c
  [[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN:-}" ]] && { printf '%s' "$LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN"; return; }
  for c in $(type -aP bats 2>/dev/null); do case "$c" in */libexec/*) ;; *) printf '%s' "$c"; return ;; esac; done
  printf '%s' "$HOME/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats"
}
BATS_BIN="$(find_bats)"
# The python3 that runs pytest for the grader: the one on PATH (actions/setup-python on CI, the
# system interpreter here), never a hard-coded /usr/bin/python3.
PY3_BIN="$(command -v python3)"

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  GRADER="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh"
  SMOKE="$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ag.XXXXXX")"
  S="$T/suite"
  export LOA_EVAL_ALLOW_HOST_GRADING=1   # grader 1.2.0 (LOW-A1): host mode is opt-in; AG-28 unsets it
  make_bin
  make_bf_py
  make_bf_sh
  make_rf_py
  make_rc
}

teardown() {
  chmod -R u+rwx "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
}

make_bin() {
  local ub
  ub="$(python3 -c 'import site; print(site.getuserbase())')"
  mkdir -p "$T/bin" "$T/dlog"
  cat > "$T/bin/python3" <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# the image's python3 stand-in: the image has pytest on its own path; the host's is in the user site
while [[ \$# -gt 0 ]]; do case "\$1" in -I|-s|-P) shift ;; *) break ;; esac; done
exec env PYTHONUSERBASE="$ub" "$PY3_BIN" "\$@"

exec env PYTHONUSERBASE="$ub" "$PY3_BIN" "\$@"
EOF
  if [[ -x "$BATS_BIN" ]]; then ln -s "$BATS_BIN" "$T/bin/bats"; fi   # absent → the bats-graded cases skip in their own setup
  cat > "$T/docker" <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
export DOCKER_STUB_LOG="$T/dlog" DOCKER_STUB_PATH="$T/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"
[[ -f "$T/docker.env" ]] && { set -a; . "$T/docker.env"; set +a; }
exec "$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/docker-stub.sh" "\$@"
EOF
  chmod +x "$T/bin/python3" "$T/docker"
}

# bf-py: the smoke slug task plus pytest.ini, a fixture test and a regression command
make_bf_py() {
  local d="$S/tasks/bf-py"
  mkdir -p "$d/fixture" "$d/hidden/tests"
  cp -a "$SMOKE/smoke-build-01/fixture/." "$d/fixture/"
  printf '[pytest]\n' > "$d/fixture/pytest.ini"
  printf 'from textkit.slug import slugify\n\n\ndef test_existing_one():\n    assert slugify("A") == "a"\n\n\ndef test_existing_two():\n    assert slugify("a b") == "a-b"\n' \
    > "$d/fixture/tests/test_existing.py"
  cp "$SMOKE/smoke-build-01/hidden/tests/test_slug.py" "$d/hidden/tests/"
  cp "$SMOKE/smoke-build-01/hidden/reference.patch" "$d/hidden/"
  echo '{"files": [{"src": "tests/test_slug.py", "dest": "tests/test_slug.py"}]}' > "$d/hidden/manifest.json"
  printf 'Fix the slug helper.\n' > "$d/TASK.md"
  cat > "$d/task.yaml" <<'YAML'
id: bf-py
schema_version: 1
type: bug-fix
fixture: tasks/bf-py/fixture
criterion: "runs of separators become one hyphen"
test_command: ["python3", "-m", "pytest", "-q", "tests"]
regression_command: ["python3", "-m", "pytest", "-q", "tests/test_existing.py"]
reference_patch: hidden/reference.patch
grader_protected: [tests/conftest.py, pytest.ini]
structural_check: null
review_catch: null
suite_version: 1
YAML
}

# bf-sh: a bash tool with bats tests, a bats helper and a Makefile target
make_bf_sh() {
  local d="$S/tasks/bf-sh" w="$T/w-sh"
  mkdir -p "$d/fixture/lib" "$d/fixture/tests" "$d/hidden/tests"
  printf 'greet() { echo "hello $1"; }\n' > "$d/fixture/lib/greet.sh"
  printf 'load_lib() { source "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../lib/greet.sh"; }\n' > "$d/fixture/tests/helpers.bash"
  printf 'test:\n\tbats tests\n' > "$d/fixture/Makefile"
  cat > "$d/hidden/tests/greet.bats" <<'EOF'
setup() { load helpers; load_lib; }

sg() { local rd="$1"; shift; git -C "$rd/sandbox" -c user.email=e@l -c user.name=eval -c commit.gpgsign=false "$@"; }

# make_run <task-id> <run-dir>: the task fixture (or the PR under pr/) committed as base
make_run() {
  local id="$1" rd="$2" td="$S/tasks/$1"
  mkdir -p "$rd/sandbox" "$rd/snapshots" "$rd/transcripts" "$rd/eval" "$rd/meta"
  echo "$id" > "$rd.task"   # beside the run dir, for apply_ref
  if [[ -d "$td/fixture" ]]; then cp -a "$td/fixture/." "$rd/sandbox/"
  else mkdir -p "$rd/sandbox/pr"; cp -a "$T/prs/pr-77/." "$rd/sandbox/pr/"; fi
  sg "$rd" init -q
  printf '%s\n' '/.claude/' '/CLAUDE.md' '/.loa.config.yaml' '/grimoires/' '/.run/' '/.beads/' '/.eval/' >> "$rd/sandbox/.git/info/exclude"
  sg "$rd" add -A; sg "$rd" commit -q --allow-empty -m base
  jq -n --arg b "$(sg "$rd" rev-parse HEAD)" '{base: $b}' > "$rd/snapshots/index.json"
  mkdir -p "$rd/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1" "$rd/sandbox/.claude"
  echo "# mount" > "$rd/sandbox/CLAUDE.md"
  printf '{"run_id": "r-%s", "status": "completed", "arm": "a1_full"}\n' "$id" > "$rd/meta/pipeline.json"
  echo a1_full > "$rd/meta/arm"
}
# snap <run-dir> <LABEL>: commit and bundle the sandbox as pipeline-run.sh does after IMPLEMENT / FIX
snap() {
  local rd="$1" L="$2" c k
  sg "$rd" add -A; sg "$rd" commit -q --allow-empty -m "snapshot $L"
  c="$(sg "$rd" rev-parse HEAD)"; k="$(printf '%s' "$L" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
  sg "$rd" bundle create -q "$rd/snapshots/$L.bundle" HEAD
  jq --arg k "$k" --arg c "$c" '.[$k] = $c' "$rd/snapshots/index.json" > "$rd/snapshots/i.tmp" && mv "$rd/snapshots/i.tmp" "$rd/snapshots/index.json"
}
# verdict <run-dir> review|audit <VERDICT> [body]
verdict() {
  local f=engineer-feedback.md; [[ "$2" == audit ]] && f=auditor-sprint-feedback.md
  printf '# Feedback\n\n%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":1}} -->\n' "${4:-}" "$2" "$3" \
    > "$1/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/$f"

tool_use() {
  jq -cn --arg t "$3" --argjson i "$4" '{type: "assistant", message: {content: [{type: "tool_use", name: $t, input: $i}]}}' \

grade() { run "$GRADER" "$@" --suite-root "$S" --allow-unfrozen --docker-bin "$T/docker"; }
tree_digest() {
  python3 -I -c '
import hashlib, os, sys
h = hashlib.sha256(); root = sys.argv[1]

+SKILL.md Phase 1C names the gate, the hook, the override and the invocation. This file carries
+the merge rules and the failed-run record.
+The dissenter receives the diff only — never `--context-file` with your Phase 1A/1B findings —
+so it evaluates the code without anchoring on your conclusions.
+1. CRITICAL/HIGH findings go into the audit report as findings of your own (they may change the
+   verdict and must appear in the Phase 2.5 tally).
+2. MEDIUM/LOW findings go under a "Cross-Model Security Observations" section.
+3. A dissenter finding that duplicates one of yours is marked "Confirmed by cross-model review".

+`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):
+before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):
+- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.

+- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.

+- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.

+- **`workdir_unavailable`, `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed`** (the range's `git diff` failed — e.g. a base ref a shallow clone lacks; `workdir_unavailable` with `metadata.path` is a previous round's file that could not be moved aside — make the a2a directory writable; written BEFORE the run lock, or with it released; non-zero exit, stdout only; nothing moved aside, so any envelope at the path is the PREVIOUS run's and never this round's evidence) — record it: `--record-fallback <the status> --reason "<its stdout line>" --since <the run started time>` (it never displaces an envelope written after that) moves that envelope and its `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` sidecars aside as `<name>.prev` (as a run does at start) before it writes, so `verdict-derive.sh` judges this round's record, not the last round's.

+A record names what it moved aside (`metadata.displaced`: status, timestamp, findings, rejected); `verdict-derive.sh` warns when that held findings. `verdict-derive.sh` never scans `.prev` files (they are the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback) and reports `.prev` files with NO envelope as a `dissent_aborted` violation, which a fallback record clears; `rejected_sidecars: []` does not silence a canonical `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` beside it — that is this run's own partial work, counted whether listed or not: triage its rows under `## Rejected dissent payloads`.
+Then set a `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker in the audit report. Empty
+findings from a run that completed are a normal pass, not a degraded review.
+A bare `planned: false` (the block opted out, `companion_voice: false`) is the operator's choice, not a degradation.
+Otherwise a completed run is still a degraded audit when its second voice is missing: `companion_voice.status` `failed`
+or `fold_failed`, `counted_as` `duplicate_voice` or `sole_voice`, or `planned: false` WITH a `reason` (a companion that
+never started: `no_workdir`, `no_route`, `prompt_copy_failed`) — set the `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker and name the
+reason. On a host with no route to the other family at all (`no_route`: no key and no CLI for it) that marker is set on
+every audit; `companion_voice: false` on the block is the operator's way to say one voice is the host's shape.
+## Two voices and the rejected-payload contract (cycle-126 FR-2)
+**Companion voice (D-2.1).** Every dissent plans a second chain from the *other* provider
+family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,
+Google, xAI, unknown) gets the Anthropic chain (`opus` → `claude-headless`), an Anthropic-family primary gets the OpenAI chain
+(`gpt-5.5` → `codex-headless`; KF-002 keeps `gpt-5.5-pro` out of the default). Credential *presence* (env → `.env.local` →
+`.env`; the value is never read) decides only where the companion chain starts — with no key it
+starts at the CLI hop. Both chains walk in parallel; the two completed envelopes are aggregated
+`failed` or `fold_failed`; `verdict_quality.voices_planned` counts the aggregated envelopes — 2 whenever the companion ran,
+completed or not (a failed one is listed in `voices_dropped`) — except a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's
+succeeded voices: INV-5 lets it feed no envelope, so `voices_planned` stays 1 and `companion_voice` is its only record; a `duplicate_voice` companion contributes none, and a
+dropped entry naming the model the companion answered with is removed (INV-5). `companion_voice.counted_as`
+(`independent_voice`, `duplicate_voice`, `sole_voice` — the primary never answered) names the outcome, and `planned: false` with a `reason` (`no_workdir`, `no_route`,
+`prompt_copy_failed`) is a companion that never started; a bare `planned: false` is the opt-out. The
+companion's findings arrive re-numbered `DISS-C-NNN` with a `voice` field; the primary's carry
+`voice` too. `metadata.companion_voice` records `{planned, family, family_basis, chain, model,
+cost_cents, attempts}`; a companion whose chain fails is a dropped voice (degraded for an audit,

+  lists the sidecars it produced; a run that writes its envelope drops the `.prev` files; a run that aborts leaves NO envelope
+  at the path and the `.prev` files beside it (the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback);
+  `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_RUN_TAG` scopes the NAMES — `adversarial-rejected-<gate>[-companion][-<tag>].jsonl` — so a chunk driver
+  passes its chunk key and nothing is renamed afterwards (a tag outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` becomes a short hash of its
+  raw value, said once, so distinct tags never share a file). A non-empty sidecar a listing envelope does not name is never
+  silent whatever its age: its rows count toward the section and a warning names the file (newer than the envelope: the
+  envelope may be stale — re-run; older: an earlier run's rows that were never folded — triage them or remove the file; a
+  chunk driver clears the directory's rejected set at the start of a round). Without an envelope, or without that field,
+  every `adversarial-rejected-<gate>*.jsonl` beside the envelope's place counts. A pre-FR-2 envelope (no metadata at all,
+  or a metadata without a `rejected_summary` key and without any FR-2 marker — `rejected_sidecars`, `companion_voice`;
+  never `rejected_count`, which the writer before cycle-126 set too) counts none of the rows as old as itself, with a
+  warning — historical sprints keep their verdicts — but a sidecar NEWER than it counts (one git tracks with its committed
+  bytes is history, whatever mtime a checkout gave it). Rows whose repair succeeded
+  never count; a trailer-less file is held to the contract too; the same section with one top-level bullet per payload
+- **Wait cap and reaping (`failure_class: timeout`).** The second voice is reaped on INT/TERM/EXIT (one cleanup trap for
+  the whole run, the whole process tree — re-collected after the freeze and before KILL — TERM then KILL after
+  `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REAP_GRACE_SECONDS`, the companion's pid trusted only while its start token matches the one recorded at
+  the fork) and by a wait cap measured from its start: each `*-headless` hop counts the CLI adapter's bound — connect +
+  max(600 s, the catalog's per-model `headless_timeout_seconds`, CLI hops only, capped at 3,600 s when the catalog loads;
+  `claude-headless` carries 900 s because a dissent on `claude -p` takes 6–10 minutes; `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_CLI_HOP_TIMEOUT` is

+  the fallback for a hop no catalog lists; a listed hop without the key is bound by the formula, 610 s) — each HTTP hop `timeout_seconds`, plus its lock wait and the CLI bound when its catalog chain falls through to a CLI
+  hop (it takes that binary's lock before its request, as a `queue` phase; cheval walks the chain inside one call), plus
+  30 s (`LOA_ADVERSARIAL_COMPANION_WAIT_SECONDS` pins it). The deadline follows the companion's phase (queue → hop → post) under a global ceiling; the post-hop work
+  (validation, repair round-trips) has its own budget, so a model that answered is never reaped mid-processing; the
+  primary's wait on a shared hop applies the same model (a companion in `post` on another hop frees the hop at once; on
+  the shared hop the primary waits for the settled record). The previous run's envelope and sidecars are moved aside at
+  start (`.prev`) and never restored — see "Rejected rows". Every
+  numeric knob (`timeout_seconds`, the context-escalation sizes, the operator seconds) is a whole number
+  without a leading zero, or its default applies with a warning — except `budget_cents` / `--budget`, which fail closed
+- **Locks.** `*-headless` hops — the dissent hops, the repair round-trips, and an HTTP alias whose catalog chain falls
+  through to a CLI hop — are serialised per CLI binary across the two walks (a per-user flock under
+  `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`$TMPDIR`, 0700, ours, never a symlink); a lock not acquired within the hop's bound fails that hop as
+  `lock_wait` — no request was sent (the chain walks on); a model that merely resolves to a CLI hop, and a repair, wait only their own call
+  timeout; queueing for the lock is not charged to the hop's cap; without `flock` (or a lock directory that is not ours)
+  the serialisation is off and said once per run. The queue is one hop deep by design: a chunk driver runs dissents
+  sequentially when any chain holds a `*-headless` hop. The envelope `adversarial-<gate>.json` and the two sidecars are
+  single-writer per (sprint, gate) — the tag scopes the sidecar names only, never the envelope — so a second live run for
+  the same sprint and gate is refused before it removes anything (`status: refused_concurrent_run` under `--json`; a
+  dead run's lock is taken over; the token is the acquiring pid and its start time; a lock directory with no token yet is a
+  holder in flight for `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_RUN_LOCK_GRACE_SECONDS`, default 5). A diff that prepares to no content is refused
+  before the run lock (`status: nothing_to_review` under `--json`, exit 1, no call made); a top-priority file not even one
+  hunk of which fits the budget is sent as its PARTIAL marker alone (`0 of N hunks shown`).
+- **`failure_class` and `last_error`.** The class follows cheval's exit codes — 4 (`MISSING_API_KEY`) `auth`; 6
+  and a diagnostic saying "timed out" (cheval reports its own CLI-hop timeout as `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`) too; 5
+  (`INVALID_RESPONSE`) or a `malformed_response` status `malformed`; anything else (1: API error, provider unavailable,
+  token revoked) `model_unavailable`; a hop whose CLI lock was never acquired is `lock_wait` (no request was sent).
+  `last_error` is an allowlisted summary of the provider's own line — cheval's error
+  tokens, "timed out after Ns", HTTP / exit codes — read from the MODELINV ledger row cheval wrote for the call (the
+  model-adapter shim discards cheval's stderr; the row is matched by model, primitive and the window of the companion's
+  LAST hop, so a repair on the same model during its post phase is not its row; concurrent dissents on one host could still
+  supply each other's line — another reason drivers run sequentially), else from the last non-banner line of the
+  companion's log; it also masks bare provider-key shapes (`sk-…`, `xai-…`, `gsk_…`, `AIza…`) the shared redactor does not
+  cover. The redacted raw line is printed to stderr and stays in the `/tmp` workdir, removed on exit; the a2a directory
+  receives the envelope and the sidecars.
+- **Repairs (`repair_hops_skipped`, `repair_budget_exhausted`).** The repair round-trip walks `tiny` (with an Anthropic
+  credential) → `claude-headless` (with the binary on PATH) → the voice that answered, always last, one bounded attempt
+  each (by canonical name: a prefixed answering voice is not appended twice); a hop that failed with an explicit auth /
+  quota code is retired for the run's remaining repairs, the answering voice never; a repair skips a hop the companion is
+  running at that moment (`repair_hops_skipped` names it, once) and waits for a CLI lock only its own timeout (a hop
+  whose wait expires never ran: named `<hop>:lock_wait`, once, and no repair slot is spent); the run's
+  repairs share a wall-clock budget (`LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_BUDGET_SECONDS`, default 5 × timeout × 2 or twice the heaviest hop's charge
+  (below) plus a timeout if that is more; a hop whose estimate — twice its last observed duration, at least the timeout,
+  at most its bound — exceeds what is left is not started and is named `<hop>:over_budget`; spent, the rest are rejected
+  unrepaired and counted in `repair_budget_exhausted`, a payload none of whose hops started for want of budget among them;
+  one none of whose hops started for any other reason — every hop retired or being run by the companion — is counted in
+  `repair_skipped_no_hop`). `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL` is filtered by the retired hops too. A hop is charged by what it
+  can reach, in the repair budget and the companion's post budget alike: a `*-headless` hop its CLI bound, an HTTP alias
+  whose chain falls through to a CLI its lock wait, its timeout and that CLI's bound. A derived
+  finding id never collides with one the model supplied; the normaliser's `id_derived` / `failure_mode_derived` markers are
+  not part of the repair's byte-diff; a derived `failure_mode` shorter than 20 characters (an enumerator, an abbreviation)
+  gives way to the description's 200-character head (counted in characters, never bytes).
+- **Credentials and ledgers.** Presence resolves per alias with override precedence (env → `.env.local` → `.env`: the
+  first place that assigns a variable decides it, an empty assignment disables that alias; a provider with several
+  aliases — `GOOGLE_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` — is present when any alias resolves non-empty; the value is never
+  expanded). Both cheval invocations append to `.run/cost-ledger.jsonl` and `.run/model-invoke.jsonl` under the writers'
+  flock (issue #689), so the hash chain stays linear.
+**Repair loop (D-2.4).** The repair chain is `tiny` (when an Anthropic credential is present) →
+`claude-headless` (when the binary is on PATH) → the voice that answered, always last — one bounded
+attempt per hop, so a host with neither still repairs through its own primary; `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL`
+pins the whole chain to one model (the round-1 hardening above has the retirement, lock and budget rules).
+KF-004 evidence: the three real rejected payloads under `tests/fixtures/dissent-rejected/` now pass without a repair.
+## Numeric anchors and the budget scaling (cycle-131 FR-4)
+- **Numeric anchors (`anchor_line`, `anchor_line_end`).** Both prompts ask each voice for the head-file line the finding
+  sits on (`anchor_line`) and, for a range, its last line (`anchor_line_end`), beside the symbol `anchor` and
+  `anchor_type`. The symbol anchor stays the stable reference and stays required for high-severity findings: the
+  anchor check, `anchor_stability` and the hallucination filter key on `anchor` alone. The normaliser keeps a line only
+  as a whole number from 1 to 10,000,000, and an end only beside a kept start and at least it; any other value is
+  dropped silently, never a rejection or a repair hop. A finding with no line is unchanged. Graders (the eval harness's
+  envelope reduction) read `anchor_line` with the anchor's file as `path:line[-end]`; read them as a pointer, never as
+  is `fixed` (the default; an absent key is the shipped gate, byte for byte) or `diff`: the budget becomes
+  `min(max(budget_cents, ceil(estimate × 1.2)), budget_cents_max)` (`budget_cents_max` default 600), where the estimate
+  is the gate's own pre-dispatch estimate over the planned voices. An estimate above that budget still refuses (exit 4,
+  `status: budget_exceeded`, `reason: budget`). A malformed scale or maximum is said and `fixed` applies. When the key is
+  written, the envelope's metadata carries `budget_scale`, `budget_cents_effective` and `budget_cents_max`. The eval
+  harness writes `diff` for both gates in its sandbox config; the shipped default stays `fixed`.

In a `.md` file a `## Section` containing a bash fence with a `# comment` has its scope cut at the comment (level 1 ≤ level 2), so a citation later in the same real section no longer shares the site's scope and the same-scope clause misses. Reproduced: site at line 4 of a section, citation at line 11 of the same section → detected only when the fence comment is removed. Since `defect_catch_rate` is the decision statistic and `.claude/` answer paths include many Markdown skills/docs with bash fences, the markdown branch of headers() must skip fenced blocks (track ``` / ~~~ fences).

For `diff pr/head/X X 2>&1 | wc -l` the diff segment's separator becomes `;`, the SILENT_SINK check never sees `wc`, and the command is planned as a content-printing diff; its result (`4`) is a non-empty body with no ranges, so every defect of X is marked exposed_unknown and the row leaves the oracle-exposed sensitivity (and the main read under --exclude-oracle-exposed). Verified with the extracted functions: `… 2>&1 | wc -l` → plan [('diff:left', X)] while `… | wc -l` → []. The redirection forms `N>&M` / `>&N` / `&>` must not split a segment.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1995 — repo_name_exempt exempts an occurrence whenever its unit is any substring of a fixture line, so a line consisting of just `0xHoneyJar/loa` (a heredoc body line, a bare backtick span) is exempt on every task whose PR fixture carries the token, since the bare token is trivially a substring of that fixture line. lines: +head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:272 — Markdown scope detection (MD_HDR at line 214, applied here) treats any line starting with `#` as a heading, including `# comment` lines inside fenced code blocks. In a `.md` file a `## Section` containing a bash fence with a `# comment` has its scope cut at the comment (level 1 ≤ level 2), so a citation later in the same real section no longer shares the site's scope and the same-scope clause misses. Reproduced: site at line 4 of a section, citation at line 11 of the same section → detected only when the fence comment is removed. Since `defect_catch_rate` is the decision statistic and `.claude/` answer paths include many Markdown skills/docs with bash fences, the markdown branch of headers() must skip fenced blocks (track ``` / ~~~ fences).

+head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2159 — split_segments treats every `&` outside quotes as a separator, so the ubiquitous `2>&1` (and `>&2`) splits a command into `diff … 2>`, `1`, and the next pipe stage. For `diff pr/head/X X 2>&1 | wc -l` the diff segment's separator becomes `;`, the SILENT_SINK check never sees `wc`, and the command is planned as a content-printing diff; its result (`4`) is a non-empty body with no ranges, so every defect of X is marked exposed_unknown and the row leaves the oracle-exposed sensitivity (and the main read under --exclude-oracle-exposed). Verified with the extracted functions: `… 2>&1 | wc -l` → plan [('diff:left', X)] while `… | wc -l` → []. The redirection forms `N>&M` / `>&N` / `&>` must not split a segment.

+head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1995 — repo_name_exempt exempts an occurrence whenever its unit is any substring of a fixture line, so a line consisting of just `0xHoneyJar/loa` (a heredoc body line, a bare backtick span) is exempt on every task whose PR fixture carries the token, since the bare token is trivially a substring of that fixture line. The KF-046 class 7 intent is quoting PR content, not the bare upstream name; require the unit to be longer than the token itself (or equal to the whole fixture line) before exempting.

I reviewed the sprint-263 PR and wrote `review.md` at the repository root with the verdict `CHANGES_REQUIRED`.

**How I checked it.** Beyond reading the full diff, I ran what was runnable from a copy of `pr/head/`: the new mount-library bats suite (11 of 11 pass, 1 skipped for a missing corpus), the recall grader bats suite (37 of 39 pass; the 2 failures only need corpus fixtures absent from the PR), the report generator on its new `c131` fixtures (all AR-48 to AR-52 expectations hold, rows validate as row writer 1.4), and took-effect's new `oracle_closed` rule end to end on a real overlaid sandbox. The row-building jq could not be exercised here because the installed jq 1.6 rejects object shorthand the base script already uses, so that is an environment limit, not a PR defect.

**Findings written to review.md:**

- **Markdown same-scope rule breaks on code fences.** The grader reads any `#`-leading line as a heading, so a `# comment` inside a fenced bash block ends the real section's scope. I reproduced a citation in the same section being missed only when the fence comment is present. This affects `defect_catch_rate`, the decision statistic, for `.md` answer paths.
- **Oracle detector splits segments on `2>&1`.** The `&` splitter turns `diff pr/head/X X 2>&1 | wc -l` into a content-printing diff, so the sink is missed and every defect of X is marked `exposed_unknown`. Verified against the extracted functions.
- **Class 7 exemption accepts the bare token.** A line that is only `0xHoneyJar/loa` is exempt on any task whose fixture mentions the repository, because it is trivially a substring of that fixture line. Low severity.

Everything else I traced held up: the budget scaling arithmetic and fail-closed config reads, the numeric-anchor jq filter on both parse paths, the pipeline wiring order, the closed-mount clauses, the report partitions and sensitivities, and the row writer's validation rules. Temporary working copies were removed and `pr/` was not modified.
